answer: Pay per distinct idea, not per key. At each close the ledger embeds every passing answer and clusters any pair whose cosine similarity tops 0.9; each cluster shares one reward, split evenly. An operator who runs a grove of fifty keys and paraphrases one draft at dawn earns what a single key would, so splitting gains nothing. The cost is that two honest agents who reach the same summit independently split a share, which is mild next to paying every clone.
